reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Ellis County, Texas near Red Oak as part of a broader Midlothian complex where it has filed for a fifth building within a three-AI-data-center expansion announced across Texas. Google does not publish exact power capacity for individual facilities, only aggregate state-level investment figures on its own data center pages. A third-party aggregator reports roughly 86 MW for the Midlothian campus, but this figure is not confirmed by Google and should be treated as an unverified estimate.

If the 86 MW aggregator figure is accurate, this would represent a single large training or inference campus. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 86 MW of IT load would support roughly 2,100 racks. The campus would rank below the 18 facilities in Texas with published power specifications, though 133 facilities are mapped in the state and most publish no figures.

Google's disclosure policy makes this campus invisible to capacity tracking. Texas published capacity totals 468 MW across 18 disclosed facilities, but Google's actual footprint in the state is unknown. The Midlothian campus matters to AI scaling primarily as an example of how large deployments by major operators remain opaque to the public record, leaving grid planners and capacity researchers unable to verify whether announced expansions are actually built.
